newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA COMPLETES WEEKEND DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA COMPLETES WEEKEND DOUBLE.

text.p: Seventeen-year-old Slovenian prodigy Primoz Peterka continued his domination of the World Cup ski jumping circuit on Sunday by registering his fifth win of the season and second in as many days.

The back-to-back wins were the first by a jumper this season. Following his victory at the prestigious Four Hills tournament last Monday, Peterka also won Saturday's event here with a massive second jump.
On Sunday Peterka was in control right from the start, posting the top jumps in both rounds to finish with a two-jump combined score of 252.90.
Finns occupied the other two places on the podium, Janne Ahonen taking second with a total of 241.20 followed by team mate Jani Soininen with 238.30.
Dieter Thoma of Germany, second in Saturday's event, was ninth after a poor first jump but moved up to fourth on the strength of his second effort, finishing with 228.00.
Peterka, in only his first full World Cup season, has displayed remarkable consistency and steely nerve, reaching the podium in eight of the last nine events.
His performance has put him solidly atop the overall standings with 832 points, comfortably ahead of Thoma in second place with 670.
